data.description:
# Epic: Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry

## Problem

The shipped attract/demo bot (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ and its follow-ups) is a
per-frame priority ladder with a reaction-time governor bolted on. It has no
commitment, no forward model, no aim/fire reasoning and no way to learn from
human play, so it reads as random and cannot be tuned into competence. We need
a **maintainable bot framework** that plays competently and human-like, adapts
to new content (enemies, power-ups, weapons) without a rewrite, can be re-run
headless for reproducible evaluation, and is backed by **telemetry** gathered
both from our own recordings and from production playtesters.

## Goals / user stories

- **As the maintainer**, I can re-run the bot headless on a fixed seed and get
  reproducible results, so I can improve it safely.
- **As the maintainer**, I can add a new enemy / power-up / weapon and have the
  bot handle it through configuration, without touching the core.
- **As the maintainer**, I can record human play and analyse it (reaction
  times, target choices, engagement distances, dodge behaviour) to tune and
  evaluate the bot.
- **As the maintainer**, I can enable opt-in telemetry in production and gather
  playtester data (state + input + events) to improve the bot and the game.
- **As a player**, I see an attract/demo mode that looks like a competent
  player.

## Design overview

- **Determinism.** A per-run **seed** drives all gameplay RNG (wave/spawn/
  timing) so a run is reproducible and the bot can be evaluated same-seed.
- **Telemetry.** A **versioned, consent-gated, pluggable** pipeline. Records
  are per-tick state + input + discrete events, tagged with the run seed and a
  schema version. Sinks: a local JSONL dev sink and a production remote sink.
  No PII; **disabled by default in production**, opt-in only.
- **Bot framework.** A world model (from `BotSnapshot`), a **registry of
  goals/behaviours**, a **utility selector with commitment/hysteresis**, a
  behaviour-tree executor, and predictive **dodge/aim** behaviours.
  Content-specific parameters live in a **config/registry** so new content is
  data, not code.
- **Evaluation.** Same-seed bot-vs-human runs, metrics, A/B comparisons and
  side-by-side clips.
- **Style matching (later).** Fit parameters or train a policy from recorded
  telemetry once the competent bot exists.

## Epic acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** Runs are reproducible from a seed; the seed is recorded in
  telemetry; a headless runner executes the bot for N ticks on a seed and
  produces a deterministic report.
- **AC2:** Telemetry is a pluggable framework with a documented, versioned
  schema, disabled by default in production and opt-in consent-gated; it
  records per-tick state + input + events with the seed and is a no-op when
  disabled.
- **AC3:** The bot is a structured framework (world model + goal/behaviour
  registry + committed selection + predictive dodge/aim), not a per-frame
  priority ladder; new enemies/power-ups/weapons are handled via config with
  tests.
- **AC4:** The competent bot completes representative runs with human-like
  behaviour (goal commitment, no suicide, human cadence) and passes an
  evaluation report (survival, minerals/min, targets engaged, dodges).
- **AC5:** Human play can be recorded and analysed offline, and a replay/ghost
  viewer compares bot vs human on the same seed.
- **AC6:** Production telemetry can be enabled by a playtester via an explicit
  opt-in, with privacy documentation and no PII.
- **AC7:** All documentation is updated (framework, extension guide, telemetry
  schema/privacy); full suite, typecheck and build pass.

## Out of scope (this epic)

- A fully style-matched clone of a specific player (style matching is an
  early-phase deliverable; full fidelity is a later follow-up).
- Server-side ML training infrastructure or online multiplayer.
- CI wiring of the capture/eval jobs (follow-up once the harness exists).

## Children (dependency order)

1. Deterministic run seeding + seed plumbing.
2. Telemetry framework (versioned schema, pluggable sinks, consent flag).
3. Game telemetry instrumentation (per-tick state + events).
4. Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling.
5. Bot framework core (world model, goal/behaviour registry, committed policy,
   content config).
6. Structured competent bot (utility goals + behaviour tree + predictive
   dodge/aim).
7. Content-adaptive configuration for enemies, power-ups and weapons.
8. Same-seed evaluation harness (metrics, A/B, side-by-side clips).
9. Style matching from telemetry (parameter fitting / imitation).
10. Production telemetry (opt-in consent, privacy, remote sink, docs).

## Related work

Builds on AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ (Smart capture bot) and its follow-ups
AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB (human-like input) and AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L (movement
goals). Supersedes the per-frame priority-ladder design.
data.title: Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry

## Summary
Dev tooling to record a human session, analyse it offline and replay/ghost it against the bot — the data loop for tuning and evaluating the bot.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A dev command/mode records a human session to JSONL (state + input + events + seed) using the telemetry framework.
- AC2: An offline analysis script produces a report: key-hold duration histogram, input-change cadence, reaction latency proxy, target-choice stats (mineral/power-up/enemy), engagement distances, dodge outcomes, survival/minerals-per-minute.
- AC3: A replay/ghost viewer steps a recording deterministically and overlays human vs bot input/position (same seed).
- AC4: The recorded dataset is versioned and documented so scripts can evolve with the schema.
- AC5: Tests for the analyser (pure stats) and the replay stepping.
- AC6: Docs: how to record, analyse and replay.
data.title: Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling

data.description:
## Summary
Implement the **competent** structured bot on top of the framework: utility-based goal selection with commitment, behaviour-tree execution (seek → line up → engage/collect → dodge), explicit aim/fire reasoning and predictive dodging. Competent first; style matching comes later.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: Goal set covering the operator's order (minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids) plus survival, each as a registered goal with a utility/priority and hysteresis.
- AC2: Behaviours: collect (approach + scoop), engage enemy, engage asteroid, evade (predictive path-around, not just direction rejection), reposition/idle.
- AC3: **Aim/fire reasoning**: the bot positions to line up a target while dodging, rather than only aiming by accident of movement.
- AC4: Survival is a hard constraint: never-suicide property tests over sampled snapshots; no wall/enemy/bullet/asteroid collision when a safe alternative exists.
- AC5: Human-like cadence: committed input changes no faster than the human-like toggles; tunables single-sourced.
- AC6: The competent bot completes a representative run (survives/destroys enough) and beats the old ladder on an evaluation metric.
- AC7: Deterministic unit tests per goal/behaviour; integration test on a seeded run.
- AC8: Docs updated (the new decision model).
data.title: Structured competent bot: utility goals, behaviour tree, predictive dodge/aim

data.description:
## Summary
Make the bot **content-adaptive**: new enemies, power-ups and weapons should be handled via configuration, not core changes, so the bot keeps working as the game grows.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A content config/registry describes, per enemy archetype, threat value, preferred engagement range, aim/lead behaviour and whether it is an asteroid-like hazard.
- AC2: Power-up and weapon definitions declare bot-relevant value/priority (e.g. collection desirability) consumed by the goal scorer.
- AC3: Adding a new enemy/power-up/weapon requires only a config entry (plus its game data) — demonstrated by a test that registers a synthetic content type and the bot handles it.
- AC4: Unknown content degrades gracefully (documented default).
- AC5: Unit tests for the config lookup and the synthetic-content path.
- AC6: Docs: "how to teach the bot about new content".
data.title: Content-adaptive configuration for enemies, power-ups and weapons

data.description:
## Summary
A reproducible evaluation harness: run the bot (and replay a human recording) on the same seed, produce metrics, A/B two bot versions, and render side-by-side clips. This is how we "re-run the bot production code" after changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A headless runner executes the bot for N ticks/seeds and emits a deterministic report (from telemetry).
- AC2: Same-seed comparison: bot vs human recording, and bot-vs-bot across versions, with metrics (survival time, minerals/min, power-ups, enemies/asteroids destroyed, avoidable hits, input cadence).
- AC3: A/B runner compares two bot configs/versions and reports the difference with confidence (multiple seeds).
- AC4: Optional side-by-side video via the existing capture tooling.
- AC5: Results are reproducible (same seed + config → same report) and stored as artifacts.
- AC6: Tests for the runner/report (pure aggregation) and determinism.
- AC7: Docs: how to run evaluations and interpret the report.
data.title: Same-seed evaluation harness: metrics, A/B, side-by-side

data.description:
## Summary
Later phase: make the bot **match a player's style** using recorded telemetry (parameter fitting and/or behaviour cloning), on top of the competent framework.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A pipeline that extracts style features from human recordings (reaction latency, hold distribution, target preferences, engagement distances, risk appetite).
- AC2: A parameter-fitting path that maps those features onto the structured bot's tunables (preferred first; keeps safety guarantees).
- AC3: (Optional/stretch) A behaviour-cloning policy trained from `(state → input)` pairs, evaluated against the structured bot on the same seeds.
- AC4: Evaluation shows the styled bot is measurably closer to the human recording than the default competent bot, without regressing competence/survival.
- AC5: Docs: how to train/fit and evaluate a style.
- AC6: Tests for the feature extraction (pure).

## Notes
Depends on the recording/analysis tooling and the evaluation harness. Lower priority than competence.
data.title: Style matching from telemetry (parameter fitting / imitation)

data.description:
## Summary
Turn on telemetry in **production** for playtesters: an explicit opt-in consent flow, privacy-safe records, batched upload to a remote sink, and documentation.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: An in-game consent/opt-in prompt (and a settings toggle) gating production telemetry; default **off**; easy opt-out.
- AC2: A remote sink that batches and uploads records (endpoint configurable), with retry/backoff and no gameplay impact when offline.
- AC3: Records are PII-free and documented; a data-retention/privacy note is included in the docs and (if applicable) the consent screen.
- AC4: A remote-off/no-op path so local dev and offline play are unaffected (tests).
- AC5: A simple way to inspect downloaded telemetry (reuse the analysis tooling from child 4).
- AC6: Tests for consent gating, the uploader's batching/backoff, and the disabled path.
- AC7: Docs: telemetry privacy + how playtester data is stored and used.
data.title: Production telemetry: opt-in consent, privacy, remote sink

## Problem

`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` test **AC4 — the victory celebration is destroyed on SHUTDOWN (no leaks)** (around line 3864) failed once during a full-suite run on 2026-10-07 while the machine was under heavy multi-agent load, then passed on an immediate re-run.

The test waits a real `VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS + 500` ms via `setTimeout` and then asserts the victory effects are destroyed. Under CPU/timer contention the hold can take longer, so the assertion races the transition.

- First run: `Test Files 1 failed | 151 passed`, `Tests 1 failed | 3509 passed` (failure at `PlayScene.test.ts` ~line 3883, `expect(effect.active).toBe(false)`).
- Immediate re-run: 152 files / 3510 tests passed.

## Expected behaviour

The test should be deterministic regardless of machine load (use fake timers / pump the scene clock rather than a wall-clock `setTimeout`, or wait on the scene state instead of a fixed delay).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The AC4 test no longer depends on a wall-clock `setTimeout` window that can be missed under load.
- AC2: The test passes repeatedly under load (e.g. run the full suite 3x on a loaded machine).
- AC3: No other PlayScene tests regress.

This is unrelated to the capture epic (the capture changes touch only `scripts/`).
data.title: Flaky PlayScene AC4 victory-celebration SHUTDOWN test under heavy load

data.description:
## Goal

Make the stored **Teleport** power-up activate **automatically**, the same way **Phase Shift** already does, instead of requiring a manual **S / ↓** key press. This removes the S / ↓ key conflict that blocks the reverse thruster (AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG) and frees S / ↓ for held reverse thrust.

## User story

As a player, when a hostile threat closes in and I hold a stored Teleport, I want the teleport to fire automatically (like Phase Shift) so I am not required to reach for a key in the middle of dodging — and so movement keys are never overloaded with a consumable ability.

## Background / existing state

- **Phase Shift already auto-triggers** through the shared, single code path: `CombatScene._updatePhaseShiftAutoTrigger(dt)` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`) calls the pure `isInDanger(player, bodies, bullets)` helper (`src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts`; danger when the combined hostile-threat count within `DANGER_RADIUS` is >= 3) and feeds the result to `EffectsRegistry.updateDanger(inDanger, dt)` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`). The registry handles charge availability, re-arm-on-danger-cleared and a post-trigger cooldown, and plays the Phase Shift cue on activation. Every combat scene (game + gyms) calls this once per frame.
- **Teleport is manual:** `CombatScene._handleTeleport()` fires on `JustDown(teleportKey)` or the hardcoded ↓ fallback and calls `triggerTeleport()`, which consumes one stored Teleport stack (FIFO) and warps the player to the nearest safe spot along the heading, granting Phase Shift on arrival. Documented in GDD §4.4 / controls table as **S / ↓**.

## Expected behaviour

- Teleport auto-activates when the player is **in danger** (same danger definition/feed as Phase Shift) **and** a stored Teleport charge exists **and** the re-arm conditions are met (danger cleared since last trigger, cooldown elapsed) — mirroring the Phase Shift auto-trigger contract.
- Manual S / ↓ activation is **removed**; S / ↓ becomes available for the reverse thruster (AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG).
- Teleport keeps its existing trigger path: nearest safe spot in the direction of travel, consuming one FIFO stack, granting Phase Shift on arrival, and the existing Phase Shift activation cue plays.
- One shared implementation in the combat core so the game and every gym behave identically (gym↔game parity).

## Acceptance Criteria (draft — to be finalised by this item's own intake)

1. Teleport auto-activates via the shared danger feed when the ship is in danger, a Teleport stack is available, and the re-arm conditions (danger cleared + cooldown) are satisfied.
2. No manual S / ↓ (or `layerDrop`) activation of Teleport remains in the game or gyms; the ↓ fallback key is removed.
3. A stored Teleport is consumed exactly once per activation; stacking/FIFO semantics are unchanged.
4. The trigger uses the existing safe-spot + Phase Shift-on-arrival path; game and gyms share one implementation (gym↔game parity).
5. The re-arm/cooldown behaviour matches the documented Phase Shift model.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the change (GDD controls table, §4.4, any UI/HUD hints, code comments) — including the removal of S / ↓ for teleport.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes, with new/updated tests covering the auto-trigger, re-arm, and no-manual-key contracts.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — replace `_handleTeleport`/`teleportKey`/`downKey` with an automatic trigger fed by the shared danger feed.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — add Teleport auto-trigger state (charge check, re-arm, cooldown) alongside the Phase Shift model.
- `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts` — reused as-is (shared danger signal).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` / `src/scenes/gym/*` — remove manual key wiring; ensure the shared auto-trigger runs.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — update the controls table and §4.4.
- Tests: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/scenes/RebindableControls.test.ts`.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Risk:** auto-teleport may fire more often than a player wants (each stored teleport is precious). Mitigation: match the Phase Shift re-arm/cooldown contract and make the trigger threshold explicit and testable.
- **Assumption:** "like Phase Shift" means the same danger-based auto-trigger model (not a timer), and the manual binding is removed entirely.
- **Blocker for:** AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG (reverse thruster on S / ↓).
data.title: Make Teleport automatic like Phase Shift (free S / Down for reverse thrust)

# Retune boss HP to 200 and screen-fix the health bar

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want the Central AI boss to require 200 hits total (readable as 4 phases of 50) and I want its health bar pinned to the top of the screen so I can always read my progress regardless of where the boss is.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering parent AC1 and AC4.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Boss.ts`: `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE = 100` and `_totalHp = BOSS_PHASE_COUNT * BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE` (400 total). Doc comment and `BossConfig.initialHp` comment reference 400/100.
- `healthBarGraphics` is created with `scene.add.graphics()`, then `this.add(this.healthBarGraphics)` puts it in the boss **container**, so it renders offset by the boss position even though `_drawHealthBar()` uses screen coordinates and `setScrollFactor(0)`.
- `getHpFraction()` is already proportional and the four phase-segment dividers already exist — keep both.

## Desired change

1. Change `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE` to `50`; total becomes **200**. Update every comment/constant reference from 100/400 to 50/200 (including `BossConfig.initialHp` docs).
2. Remove the `this.add(this.healthBarGraphics)` container membership so the bar is a **scene child** (it is already created via `scene.add.graphics()`); keep `setScrollFactor(0)` and `setDepth(100)`. It now renders at the absolute screen coordinates drawn by `_drawHealthBar()` (horizontally centred at `BOSS_HEALTH_BAR_Y`).
3. Keep the proportional fill and the four phase-segment dividers.
4. Ensure `destroy()` still explicitly destroys `healthBarGraphics`.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — HP constants/comments, health-bar re-parenting.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts` — health-model and health-bar placement tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — gym health-bar placement expectations.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — health-bar layering assumptions if any.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE === 50` and total HP is 200; hitting 49 times keeps phase 1, the 50th hit advances to phase 2, and the 200th hit destroys the boss.
- The health bar Graphics is **not** a child of the boss container and its screen position is unchanged when the boss position changes (assert `boss.x`/`boss.y` separately from the bar's drawn position).
- `getHpFraction()` decreases monotonically with each hit from 1.0 toward 0.
- The four phase-segment dividers and the proportional fill are retained.
- All `Boss.test.ts` / `GymBoss.test.ts` assertions updated for 200 HP pass.

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC1) **Boss total health is 200.** The boss spawns with 200 total hits across the existing **4 phases (50 hits per phase)**. The 4-phase structure, phase transitions, and score/minion rewards gated on *depleting* hits are preserved. Verified by unit tests: hit 49 stays in phase 1, hit 50 advances to phase 2, and hit 200 destroys the boss.
- (parent AC4) **The health bar is fixed at the top of the screen and decreases per hit.** The bar is camera-fixed, horizontally centred at the top of the playfield, always visible during the encounter, and **not** offset or moved by the boss's figure-8 motion. Its fill shrinks proportionally on every hit (200 → 0) with the four phase-segment dividers retained. Verified by tests asserting the bar's screen position is independent of the boss position and that `getHpFraction()` decreases after hits.
data.title: Retune boss HP to 200 and screen-fix the health bar

# Add dedicated boss-hit SFX cue

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want a distinct, punchy sound on every boss hit so hits feel responsive and obviously register.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering the SFX half of parent AC5.

## Existing state

- `src/audio/effects.ts` exposes the boss cues (`playBossFireSound`, etc.) via the shared ToneForge playback layer.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` maps every sound-producing cue to a recipe (baked/existing-recipe/runtime-shim) and seeds; `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` is the typed runtime view; `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts` enforces completeness.
- Baked WAVs live in `public/audio/sfx/` and are **tracked in git**; recipes live in `audio/toneforge/recipes/`.

## Desired change

1. Add a new recipe `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-boss-hit.yaml` producing a short, punchy boss-hit impact (model the YAML shape on `aihell-boss-fire.yaml`).
2. Add a new baked manifest entry in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`: `{ "cue": "playBossHitSound", "recipe": "aihell-boss-hit", "delivery": "baked", "seeds": [<new seed>] }`.
3. Add `playBossHitSound()` to `src/audio/effects.ts` (delegating to `playCue`).
4. Render and commit the baked WAV `public/audio/sfx/aihell-boss-hit.<seed>.wav` via the documented audio build pipeline (`scripts/build-audio.sh` / ToneForge).
5. Add/extend the cue-manifest contract test to require `playBossHitSound`.

## Key Files

- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-boss-hit.yaml` (new).
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — new cue entry + seed.
- `public/audio/sfx/aihell-boss-hit.<seed>.wav` (new, committed).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playBossHitSound()`.
- `src/audio/cueManifest.ts`, `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts` — mapping/contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `playBossHitSound` is exported from `src/audio/effects.ts` and appears in `CUE_MANIFEST` with recipe `aihell-boss-hit` and delivery `baked`.
- The recipe YAML exists, is valid, and the baked WAV for its seed is present under `public/audio/sfx/` and tracked.
- The cue-manifest contract test passes and fails if `playBossHitSound` is removed.
- No new runtime dependency is added.
data.title: Add dedicated boss-hit SFX cue

# Implement on-screen action intensity metric (recording + video join)

**Sibling epic** of the research/decision item [Screen action intensity
tracking and analysis (AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN)] —
`discovered-from:AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN`. Created by that item's AC5. This is a
sibling (not a child) so the research item can close once its decision is
recorded without waiting for implementation.

## Goal

Implement the hybrid layered `actionIntensity` metric decided in
`docs/dev/action-intensity.md`: a pure, deterministic, O(entities) score of
on-screen presence + event bursts, recorded through the existing telemetry
pipeline, serialised as a versioned time series, and joinable to captured
WebM for highlight selection.

## User stories

- **As a game designer**, I can view a time-series of on-screen action
  intensity for a run, so I can evaluate pacing and find boring or
  over-crowded segments.
- **As a video editor**, I can map action-intensity peaks to captured-video
  timestamps and auto-select highlight clips.
- **As a maintainer**, the metric is computed once in the shared core and
  consumed identically by the game and the gyms, and reuses the telemetry
  pipeline rather than a parallel instrumentation path.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Pure core module.** A pure `computeActionIntensity(state, config)`
  lives in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`), is O(entities) + O(1) per
  event, introduces no RNG, and returns the sample shape (rawScore,
  intensity, smoothed, burstiness, per-category breakdown) defined in the
  decision document §7.1. Unit-tested hermetically (no browser).
- **AC2 — Config.** All knobs (per-category weights incl. the refined
  player-bullet 0.5 and asteroids 1.0; `cap_c`; event window `W`; reference
  budget `B`; blend `k_E`; half-life `h`; sample rate) are config-driven with
  the decision-document defaults, and documented at the definition site.
- **AC3 — Telemetry integration.** The metric is wired into the per-tick
  telemetry `state` via the instrumentation child (AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH),
  reusing the `BotSnapshot` builder's registries. Recording is a **strict
  no-op when telemetry is disabled** (zero records, no allocation). No new
  schema bump is required (payload-only change); the shape is documented in
  `docs/TELEMETRY.md`.
- **AC4 — Event-window layer.** The burst layer consumes the discrete events
  the instrumentation child records (`enemy_killed`, `player_hit`,
  `boss_phase`, `powerup_collected`, `wave_clear`), with the documented
  default event values; verified by tests over a seeded event sequence.
- **AC5 — Derived time series.** A tooling-side serialiser emits the
  standalone JSONL artefact (`schemaVersion`, `runSeed`, `sampleRateHz`,
  `categories` header + one sample per line, `t` in ms since run start) to a
  git-ignored location alongside the capture output, with a matching
  basename. Round-trip tested.
- **AC6 — Video join + highlight selection.** A dev-gated `capture_started`
  marker (epoch ms, `import.meta.env.DEV`) is emitted at recording start; a
  helper maps `t` to video time using the shared anchor and returns merged
  highlight windows from the documented thresholds. Pure and unit-tested.
- **AC7 — Gym↔game parity.** The counter is authored once in the shared core
  and consumed by `PlayScene` and the gym scenes; the duplicate-body guard
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still passes. A single
  count-able registry (or per-kind live counters) exists for enemy/boss
  explosion VFX so categories are not double-counted.
- **AC8 — Docs & tests.** `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` is cross-linked from
  `README.md` and `docs/TELEMETRY.md`; the full suite, typecheck and build
  pass; no shipped-bundle impact (`npm run check-bundle` passes).

## Dependencies

- **Epic AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4** — Realistic demo/attract bot framework +
  playtester telemetry (must be at least `high`; verified).
- **AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO** — Telemetry framework: versioned schema, pluggable
  sinks, consent flag (provides the envelope/sinks; completed).
- **AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH** — Game telemetry instrumentation: per-tick state and
  events (canonical integration point; `actionIntensity` field lives here).
- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** — Automated gameplay capture spike (video consumer
  for the join).

Implementation must wait for AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH's tick-state integration
point to land (or land first if sequenced ahead of it).

## Key files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — the decision this epic implements.
- `src/scenes/core/` — new pure `actionIntensity` module + config (+ tests).
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — existing registries the metric reads.
- `src/telemetry/` — recorder integration (via AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH);
  `docs/TELEMETRY.md` schema note.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` / `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` —
  `capture_started` marker + highlight-selection helper.
- `README.md` — cross-link to the decision document.

## Out of scope

- Driving pacing / adaptive difficulty from the metric (separate consumer
  work item).
- Calibration against human/physiological data (separate follow-up; required
  before the metric drives difficulty).
- ML excitement prediction and automatic editing.

# Tooling: JSONL time-series serialiser

Produces the standalone JSONL artefact from recorded telemetry for analysis and video join.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC5 — Derived time series.** A tooling-side serialiser emits the standalone JSONL artefact with schemaVersion, runSeed, sampleRateHz, categories header and one sample per line.

**Key Files:**
- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensitySerialiser.ts` — new serialiser module
- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensitySerialiser.test.ts` — round-trip tests

**Implementation:**
1. Create a pure serialiser that takes the sampled telemetry records and produces JSONL.
2. Header line: `schemaVersion`, `runSeed`, `sampleRateHz`, `categories` array.
3. Sample lines: `t` (ms since run start), `tick`, `rawScore`, `intensity`, `smoothed`, `burstiness`, `breakdown`.
4. Each line carries `schemaVersion`. Output to a git-ignored location alongside capture output with matching basename.
5. Unit-test round-trip: serialise → deserialise → verify all fields preserved. Test header-only (no samples), truncated file tolerance, partial run handling.
6. Test the file naming convention: `capture-output/<run-id>.action.jsonl`.
data.title: Tooling: JSONL time-series serialiser

# Capture: video join + highlight selection

Maps action intensity timestamps to captured video and returns highlight windows.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC6 — Video join + highlight selection.** A dev-gated `capture_started` marker is emitted and a helper returns merged highlight windows from documented thresholds.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` — add `capture_started` marker (dev-gated)
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — integrate highlight helper
- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts` — pure highlight selection helper
- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.test.ts` — unit tests

**Implementation:**
1. Add a dev-gated `capture_started` epoch ms marker at the `MediaRecorder` start point in `capture-run-lifecycle.mjs`.
2. Create a pure helper: `mapTimeToVideo(t, capture_started, run_startedAt) => videoTimeMs`.
3. Create highlight window computation: read JSONL, find peak windows where `burstiness ≥ 0.15` and/or `intensity ≥ 0.7`, merge within 1.0s gap, apply lead (1.5s) / tail (1.0s).
4. All highlight logic is pure and unit-testable. No browser needed for tests.
5. Test: time mapping (with and without capture_started), highlight window detection, gap merging, boundary clamping (first sample may predate capture_started).
6. Gate all video-join code behind `import.meta.env.DEV`.
data.title: Capture: video join + highlight selection

data.comment: Design: added a content registry (src/ai/framework/content.ts) with EnemyContentProfile (threat, engagementRange, aim, asteroidLike) and DropContentProfile (value). The world model partitions asteroids via the registry asteroidLike flag; the competent goals score enemy proximity by threat and drop proximity by value; the collect/engage behaviours pick the best value-per-distance target and use each archetype's preferred engagement range/aim. Unknown archetypes/drops resolve to documented neutral defaults (threat/value 1, aim direct, non-asteroid). Shipped profiles live in competent/content.ts and a guard test fails if a game enemy/drop id lacks a profile. Assumption: aim 'lead' is accepted and documented but currently behaves as 'direct' because the read-only snapshot exposes no enemy velocity (reserved for a future predictor).
